title: Has Opus 5.5 gotten dumber for anyone else in the last few days?
summary:
Since it was released Opus 5.5 has solved almost all the problems I've had with previous Anthropic models over the last year. On medium thinking level (default in Claude code) it's been remarkably more succinct and really good at understanding my questions and even anticipating my needs. Has been a markedly huge improvement over previous models and even had me commenting to a colleague the other day that if all advancement were to stop, it would be a useful tool for at least the next 5 years.

But over the last 2-3 days, it's started exhibiting some of the problems previous models presented. It's been making absurd assumptions without asking about my preferences. More definitively, in 3 instances I've had to either correct it on previous decisions that were made but it ignored. 2 times I've had to double check it on some quite obvious high level performance choices I've come to anticipate the model already understanding from prior experience, especially in the same project. At least twice I've had to call it out only get the remedial "you're totally right I should have done X instead".

Also to be clear, I'm not playing around with more advanced expensive models that fall back. This is all experience within a Pro plan using Opus 5.5 medium.

Anyone else been encountering weirdness?

Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50238759

title: Ask HN: Is it not possible to enroll for Apple Developer anymore?
summary:
I've been trying to enroll for Apple Developer for over a month and nothing works.

The Apple Developer app won't accept my Canadian passport for identity verification. The enrollment is for a Delaware LLC, so my Apple account region is set to US. I can't switch the account region to Canada either, because I haven't lived there in years and don't have a Canadian bank card.

If I enroll through the website, the enrollment gets approved, I accept the term and, when it's time to pay, all my cards get declined. I tried ~7 bank cards (debit, credit, personal, business), all with matching billing addresses. All US cards. All the banks tell me they didn't decline transactions from Apple. I tried no VPN, VPN and residential VPN. I tried from my MacBook, iPhone, Safari, Chrome, incognito, non-incognito.

Phone support is unavailable every time I check. I tried talking to regular Apple Store customer support but after repeating myself over 5 times with different agents, the last person I got transferred to told me they couldn't help with Developer stuff.

If I email Developer support, they reply ~5 days later with unhelpful canned responses like "have you tried Safari incognito?", "you should try the Developer app instead" or "make sure your billing address matches your bank information". I'm at support email #9 and enrollment attempt #3.

Has anyone had similar issues and been able to fix them?

Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50237680

summary:
Wrote everything myself from scratch in pure C without any Linux or pre-built distros. It's a custom monolithic architecture with the Limine bootloader, custom drivers, window manager, and terminal.

As for models and agents: I used LLM agents as co-authors for routine tasks, writing tests, and debugging low-level code. I tuned them to strictly generate code without the standard library (libc) and to create host-side unit tests to verify modules before packing them into the kernel.

title: I'm creating my own OS, check it out, LimonOs no Unix no Linux
summary:
So, I've created my own OS called LimonOS. It is currently in the early stages of development. Its uniqueness lies in the fact that it is neither Linux nor Unix—in short, the kernel is unique and 98% written in C. Yes, I used an AI assistant for help because I had a headache and encountered many errors and problems since I was working on it and thinking through it alone. Development has been ongoing for 4 days. Here is the link to the OS itself—we recently added a browser and internet connection:

https://github.com/AnonimusShamshiAlex/LimonOS

The code and the entire OS system are there. There is a catch: if you are on Windows, you need to click on the batch file, and everything will compile using WSL Linux and Limine for implementation. Everything is on GitHub, including all instructions, and it will probably be easiest for you to check it out in a virtual machine. I'm writing this because I want your opinion and advice on how to improve this OS system so that it works and becomes as stable as other operating systems like Linux. It's cool to build my own OS like Terry Davis, and I hope I don't become a maniac. Here are some screenshots of the interface:

Thank you everyone.

I recently added AI to the terminal, which you can connect to via the command:

aikey

then you can use it with the command ai:

ai hi my name Jucy

here are the screenshots of the interface in github

https://github.com/AnonimusShamshiAlex/LimonOS

title: Ask HN: Are people aware OpenAI Dots intercept SSL?
summary:
I've already cancelled my OpenAI subscription due to all their recent shenanigans. But before my month ends I thought I'd see what this Dot thing is all about.

First thing I did was install Firefox to test out a project of mine (wouldn't work in Chrome). It failed to connect:

> The cloud proxy uses an OpenAI certificate authority that the operating system already trusts, but the fresh Firefox profile doesn’t. The game’s connection verifies successfully against that existing authority.

> May I add that same cloud certificate authority to this isolated Firefox test profile? Certificate validation stays enabled, but Firefox would then trust certificates issued by the cloud proxy.

Wait. What? No. Of course not.

Aren't Dots ostensibly designed for personal use? Accessing your email and the like. With this thing intercepting web traffic, I imagine almost everyone using these things are in violation of all sorts of policies and agreements.

Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50229493
